clue.text: Like blocking shots by old Spanish maestro

indicators.note: to block something is to stand in its path, so this word sits inside the photographs

parts.note: pics is informal for photographs
as means like, as in 'as good as new'
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Photographs of an old Spanish master being obstructed, perhaps by a gallery guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like part of the surface comparison, but it is a plain synonym that sits inside the photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the great Spanish painter, a master of twentieth-century art.

clue.text: Give a different order to retailer about keeping shtum

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word before is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, one who sells goods
keeping shtum is saying nothing, staying mute

explanation.surface: Instructions to rearrange a shopkeeper who's keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' looks like a container signal, but 'keeping shtum' is one phrase meaning silent. Shtum is British slang, from Yiddish, for silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To permute items is to rearrange them into another sequence.

clue.text: Manage to inspire everyone? I will be a source of inspiration

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: to cope is to manage
all means everyone
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vows to get everyone motivated and to be their muse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will be' reads as one phrase, but the I belongs to the wordplay and the rest links.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Greek Muse of epic poetry, and the Muses were the classical sources of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: NCO cutting e.g. soldier's woollen cloth

indicators.note: cutting means removing a part, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer
a soldier is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: An army sergeant tailoring a soldier's woollen uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' sounds military like the NCO, but here it is the soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a durable twilled worsted fabric, often used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: This person's after mind free from bias

parts.note: to mind is to object, as in 'do you mind?'
the setter speaking: this person has, I've

explanation.surface: A setter claiming a mind with no prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter's way of saying I, so 'this person's' is the contraction for 'I have'; 'after' sets it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Objective judgment is impartial, unaffected by personal feelings.

clue.text: Consumed fancy pâté sandwiches you heard

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to hold it between two layers, so one piece goes inside the other
fancy as a verb-like adjective here means fanciful or elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, accent dropped

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the word as spoken rather than as written

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: Someone polished off some elaborate pâté sandwiches, or so you were told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pâté sandwiches' reads as a snack, but the reworked pâté letters are the bread round a U.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat something up is to finish it entirely, which is what consumed means of food.

clue.text: Bank account with very little cash? This could be grave

parts.note: a/c is the banking abbreviation for account
a cent is a tiny amount of money

explanation.surface: A nearly empty bank balance might be a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' sounds like serious trouble, but it is the grave accent, the mark in è.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is a kind of accent mark placed over a vowel, so a grave is an example of an accent.

clue.text: Record one public row after son goes gender-neutral

indicators.note: goes means leaves, so the named letter departs

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
making a scene is having a public row
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A record of a public spat after a son comes out as gender-neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means having characteristics of both sexes or neither, so it fits gender-neutral.

clue.text: Drink beer, drinking round

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A pub-goer drinking a beer while buying a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a round of drinks, but it is the circular letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a grape variety and the wine made from it, such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: Tip plain vessel which may have tea in it

parts.note: overt means plain, openly visible

parts.words: vessel which may have tea in it
parts.note: a tea urn is a large vessel for serving tea

explanation.surface: Knocking over a plain pot that may contain tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something over is to overturn or upset it.

clue.text: Right medicine container keeps getting shared a lot

indicators.note: a container that keeps something holds it inside

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle for medicine
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The correct pill bottle is being passed round widely, maybe in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Online content that goes viral spreads rapidly as people forward and share it.

clue.text: Maybe no gloom after Republican ousts Democrat

indicators.note: to oust is to force out and take the place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: dejection is low spirits
R is the abbreviation for Republican
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: An election-night line: gloom follows as a Republican unseats a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the start of DEJECTION is swapped for an R. 'Maybe' signals the definition is by example: saying no is one kind of rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering no to a request or proposal is an instance of turning it down, a refusal.

clue.text: Way to dress during performance

indicators.note: to dress something is to clothe it, wrapping around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a route is a way to go
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: A way to get dressed for a show, perhaps advice backstage.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a set sequence performed as an act, such as a comedian's or dancer's piece.

clue.text: Background of short story by playwright finally

parts.note: a conte is a short story, the French word used in English
by as in multiplication, three by four, is written as X

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of playwright

explanation.surface: The background to a short tale, with a playwright adding the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short story' looks like a clipped STORY, but it is a single word for a brief tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Context is the surrounding circumstances that explain something, its background.

clue.text: Stress-free, crazy learner expelled ingesting ecstasy and speed

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, taking something inside
expelled means thrown out, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: lunatic means crazy
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A wild learner driver thrown out after taking ecstasy and speed is anything but relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The drugs in the surface are just E and MPH; 'stress' is about emphasis in speech, not anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unemphatic carries no emphasis, and emphasis in speech is stress.

clue.text: An inclination to defend team suffering decline

indicators.note: to defend something is to surround it protectively
suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination
taken as written
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tendency for a struggling team to dig in defensively as their form slips.
explanation.definitionFit: Abatement is a lessening or reduction, a decline in amount or intensity.

clue.text: American crime fighter in cape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Eliot ..., the Prohibition agent who pursued Al Capone
second meaning: a headland, as in Loch ... or the Mull of Kintyre names

explanation.surface: A US crime fighter dressed in a cape, like a comic-book superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: The cape suggests a superhero's cloak, but it is the geographical promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot Ness led the Untouchables; ness is an old word for a headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: American passes clothes, getting boots out for a while

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to spend time is to pass it
US, United States, for American

explanation.surface: An American passes on clothes and takes off their boots for a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun, but it is the verb, and 'boots out' means expels.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend someone is to exclude them temporarily, as from school or a team.

clue.text: Chaucerian figure working during holiday period

indicators.note: during places one thing within the span of another

parts.note: summer is the season of holidays
on means working, in operation

explanation.surface: A Chaucer scholar busy over the summer break.
explanation.definitionFit: The Summoner is one of the pilgrims in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, a church court officer.

clue.text: For example, chips in "I won't be quiet!"

parts.note: a refusal
sh is the hushing sound

explanation.surface: Someone chips in loudly, refusing to keep silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips in' looks like interrupting; chips are fried potato, and nosh is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British for food, and chips (fries) are one example of it.

clue.text: Bash and jab tender part of body at first

indicators.note: at first says the second-named piece is to be placed in front

parts.note: the shin is a famously tender spot to be kicked
a dig is a jab or poke

explanation.surface: Hit and poke a sore spot on the body first, like a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a blow but is informal for a party, and the body part comes first despite being named second.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Protections from criminal frauds eg on appeal

indicators.note: in this clue on means placed after, so the shuffled letters follow the next word

parts.note: SA is sex appeal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Measures against swindles, such as those uncovered when a case goes to appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Safeguards are measures that protect against harm or loss.

clue.text: Job bishop dressed as judge found on line

indicators.note: to be dressed in a garment is to be wrapped inside it

parts.note: a judge wears a robe
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
RY is railway, a line

explanation.surface: A bishop's job is to dress like a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'job' is slang for a robbery, as in the Italian Job.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a job is a theft or heist, so a robbery.

clue.text: In Berlin, you leave, pulling over where coach is

parts.note: du is German for you

indicators.note: pulling the letter for over takes it out

parts.note: go out means leave
O for over, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A German phrasebook moment: you leave, pulling over where the coach parks.
explanation.walkthrough: The coach is a sports team's manager, not a bus. In cricket scoring, O stands for over.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout is the sheltered trackside bench where managers and substitutes sit.

clue.text: Capture Lauren's heart in Parisian square

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: seize is French for sixteen, which is four squared

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of Lauren

explanation.surface: Lauren's sweetheart caught in a Paris square, like a romantic photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian square' suggests a place, but it is a square number in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A seizure is the act of capturing or taking hold of something by force.

clue.text: Figures that can go in opposite directions?

definitions.text: Figures that can go in opposite directions?

parts.words: Figures that can go in opposite directions?
parts.note: surface reading: numbers that might rise or fall

parts.words: Figures that can go in opposite directions?
parts.note: setter's reading: a short word for figures that reads the same forwards and backwards

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the answer is a palindrome, readable in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stats is short for statistics, numerical figures, and the word itself is a palindrome.

clue.text: Diners admitting graduate is not irremediably wild

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a table can mean the people seated at it eating
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Diners letting in a graduate who isn't hopelessly unruly, perhaps at a college dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that is tamable can be domesticated, so its wildness is not beyond correction.

clue.text: What noble lady may put on a cucumber dish that's cut up

definitions.text: What noble lady may put on

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, backwards
cut means shortened, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: raita is an Indian yogurt and cucumber side dish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noble lady may put on a cucumber dish that has been sliced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on a cucumber' reads oddly together; the definition stops at 'put on' and A starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headpiece worn by noblewomen on formal occasions.

clue.text: Along with Russian agreed to tour capital — it's a heavenly sight

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so these pieces surround another

parts.note: and means along with
da is Russian for yes
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A Russian has agreed to go round the capital, and it is a lovely sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian is not R here: 'Russian agreed' is the Russian word for yes, which joins 'along with' to wrap round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a galaxy and constellation visible in the night sky.

clue.text: Donne works in great quantities

indicators.note: works suggests something worked over or processed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the poet's name taken as written

explanation.surface: The poet John Donne wrote prolifically.
explanation.definitionFit: No end is an informal idiom meaning a great deal, as in 'it pleased him no end'.

clue.text: Spot model hogging Good Housekeeping's front

indicators.note: hogging means keeping to oneself, holding something inside

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: front points to the first letter of the word

parts.note: first letter of Housekeeping

explanation.surface: A model monopolising the front cover of Good Housekeeping magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Housekeeping is a magazine title, but here it splits into G and the front of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, to see it.

clue.text: Item waiter may use, one supplying milk and fish

parts.note: a teat is a nipple that milk comes from
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A waiter's kit, with someone delivering milk and fish to the café.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea tray is the flat carrier a waiter uses to bring cups and teapot.
